html:
John Amos Comenius was a teacher, writer and bishop of the Unity of the Brethren, born in 1592 in southeast Moravia, who is called the father of modern education.

After the White Mountain he lost his home, wife and children and in 1628 went into exile, living in Poland, Sweden, Hungary and finally Amsterdam. He argued that all children, girls and boys, rich and poor, should go to school, learn in their own language, and move from simple things to hard ones. His Orbis Pictus of 1658 was one of the first picture books for children and was used for two centuries. He also wrote The Labyrinth of the World, a classic of Czech prose. His ideas shaped later reformers, and his birthday is Teachers' Day in the Czech Republic and in Slovakia.
